resolution.how: lib/auth.js adds three independent checks run once at the dispatcher before any handler: Host must be loopback on this port (defeats DNS rebinding), Origin when present must be this daemon's own (defeats the no-preflight cross-origin POST), and x-interstice-token must match a per-daemon 0600 token compared in constant time. Page loads are the only exempt route, because serving a page is how a browser is given the token; a bootstrap in the head wraps fetch so every page request carries it. CLI, doctor and the hotkey apps read the same file.
resolution.verified: Live against the running daemon: the exact cross-origin POST the finding fired went 200 -> 403, an untokened GET 200 -> 401, a raw-socket rebound Host 200 -> 403, and a tokened GET 200. test/auth.test.js pins all of it, including the attack over a raw socket because Host is a forbidden header for fetch.
